plain: The buying and selling of goods between people and places.

webster.text: In a general sense, an interchange or mutual change of goods, wares, productions, or property of any kind, between nations or individuals, either by barter, or by purchase and sale; trade; traffick.

more.text: Intercourse between individuals; interchange of work, business, civilities or amusements; mutual dealings in common life.
Interchange; reciprocal communications; as, there is a vast commerce of ideas.

example.quote: What prudent merchant will hazard his fortunes in any new branch of commerce when he knows not but that his plans may be rendered unlawful before they can be executed?
